comment: Committed tier classification for the gold-set cells (internal/goldset/testdata), assigned before candidate results per ADR 0008. Keys are benchmark names with the -GOMAXPROCS suffix stripped. Every tier here is licensed by the checked-in classification profile at internal/perfgate/testdata/profile-30614184386 -- workflow_dispatch run 30614184386 against master at head 4607f1e, GOMAXPROCS=2, BENCHTIME=200ms, BENCH_COUNT=10. That profile's README records the measured latency, bytes, and allocation figure behind every cell's tier, and the reasoning for each one that changed. Reclassification requires a newer committed profile justifying it; a figure from a developer box licenses nothing. Control-flow and dispatch-dominated cells are engine-sensitive; rule-load is startup-shaped. guard-nil is the one gold-set cell whose latency does not move with execution mode (+2.65% on the profile), so data-dominated names its shape -- and it fails that tier because the VM allocates 19.40% more bytes than the Evaluator. That is a finding about the engine, not a tier this file can choose its way out of: no tier both describes the cell honestly and passes it. GoldsetParse/* cells (added with BenchmarkGoldsetParse, docs/profiling-baseline.md's 'Measured per-fixture parse share') measure the reader alone and are identical across execution modes by construction, so engine-sensitive is wrong for them: that tier requires a mode-driven improvement under first-authorization, which a mode-invariant cost can never show. They are classified data-dominated instead -- the reader's own cost is AST-collection construction (Tokenize/parseList/parseForm/parseVector, docs/profiling-baseline.md), and that tier's +-5% tolerance is the correct check for a cost that must not vary by mode. That check is two-sided under first-authorization, where the paired runs are the two evaluators of one commit and a mode-invariant cost moving either way is a finding; under non-regression, where the comparison is against a previous release, it bounds regression only. The committed profile measures all thirteen as not statistically significant on latency (p=0.22-0.93) and bit-identical on bytes and allocations (p=1.000), so the gate reports them INCONCLUSIVE: no tier lets a cell assert that not moving is the correct outcome. Data-dominated stays the decidable classification regardless. Under first authorization these are non-regression claims, so Resolve() collapses a still-inconclusive cell to PASS, and a cell whose latency delta is significant but small passes outright -- run 30561584997 recorded exactly that for GoldsetParse/text-render (+1.39%, p=0.033, PASS), which is the tier behaving as intended rather than an exception to it. What a positive invariance verdict would cost, and the rerun ordering that hides one today, are recorded in gate-tier-reclassification task 2.3 -- both belong to whoever next widens the gate's machinery, not to this file.
